The CPU profiler couldn't write its output file inside the sandbox. I'll time each section directly with `performance.now()` instead, without touching any files.
`isPrime` inside `countPrimes` is the slow part. In `scripts/slow.mjs`, `countPrimes(60000)` takes about 260 ms, and `dedupe(30000 values)` takes about 31 ms.

`countPrimes` calls `isPrime` on every number below 60,000. `isPrime` tries every divisor up to `n`, so each prime costs roughly `n` modulo operations, and there are about 6,000 primes below 60,000. That gives on the order of 1.6×10⁸ operations, which is most of the runtime.

I couldn't get a CPU profile because the sandbox blocked the profiler from writing its output file. The numbers above come from timing each function separately, so they're a direct measurement rather than a profile. No files were changed.
